verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah the son of Helkiah. And it came to pass in the month of Secheelu, in the twentieth year, that I was in Susa Abira.
verses.1:2: And Hanani, one of my brethren, came, he and men of Judah; and I inquired of them concerning those who had escaped, who were left from the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
verses.1:3: And they said to me, "The remaining ones who were left from the captivity there in the province, in the city, are in great distress and in reproach; and the walls of Jerusalem are torn down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
verses.1:4: And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned for days; and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
verses.1:5: And I said, "Ah, I pray, O Lord God of heaven, the mighty, the great and awesome One, who keeps the covenant and Your mercy for those who love Him and for those who keep His commandments:
verses.1:6: Let Your ear now be attentive and Your eyes be open, to hear the prayer of Your servant which I pray before You today, day and night, concerning the sons of Israel Your servants, and confessing the sins of the sons of Israel which we have sinned against You; both I and my father's house have sinned.
verses.1:7: We have utterly broken faith, and have not kept the commandments, and the statutes, and the judgments which You commanded Your servant Moses.
verses.1:8: Remember, I pray, the word which You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, 'If you break covenant, I will scatter you among the peoples;
verses.1:9: and if you turn back to Me, and keep My commandments and do them, though your dispersion be from the farthest end of heaven, from there I will gather them, and bring them to the place which I have chosen to cause My name to dwell there.'
verses.1:10: Now these are Your servants and Your people, whom You have redeemed by Your great power and by Your mighty hand.
verses.1:11: Ah, I pray, indeed let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant, and to the prayer of Your servants who desire to fear Your name; and grant prosperity, I pray, to Your servant today, and give him compassion before this man." Now I was a eunuch to the king.
verses.2:1: And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that wine was before me; and I took the wine and gave it to the king, and there was no other before him.
verses.2:2: And the king said to me, "Why is your countenance sad, when you are not unwell? This is nothing other than sorrow of heart." And I was exceedingly afraid,
verses.2:3: and I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my countenance not be sad, since the city, the house of the tombs of my fathers, has been laid waste, and its gates have been devoured by fire?"
verses.2:4: And the king said to me, "Concerning what do you make this request?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
verses.2:5: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant is pleasing before you, send him to Judah, to the city of the tombs of my fathers, and I will rebuild it."
verses.2:6: And the king said to me—the concubine also sitting beside him—"How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king, and he sent me; and I gave him an appointed time.
verses.2:7: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the River, that they may conduct me through until I come to Judah,
verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the park that belongs to the king, that he may give me timber to roof the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for the house into which I shall enter." And the king granted them to me, according to the good hand of God.
verses.2:9: Then I came to the governors beyond the River, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent with me captains of the army and horsemen.
verses.2:10: And Sanballat the Horonite heard of it, and it was grievous to them that a man had come to seek good for the sons of Israel.
verses.2:11: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
verses.2:12: And I arose in the night, I and a few men with me; and I told no one what God was putting into my heart to do with Israel, nor was there any beast with me except the beast on which I rode.
verses.2:13: And I went out by the Gate of Golela, and toward the mouth of the Spring of the Figs, and to the Dung Gate; and I was breaking at the wall of Jerusalem which they were tearing down, and its gates had been devoured by fire.
verses.2:14: Then I passed on to the Gate of Aina and to the King's Pool, and there was no room for the beast under me to pass through.
verses.2:15: And I went up along the wall of the brook by night, and I was breaking at the wall; and I was at the Valley Gate, and returned.
verses.2:16: And the guards did not know why I had gone and what I was doing; nor had I yet told the Jews, or the priests, or the nobles, or the rest who were doing the works.
verses.2:17: Then I said to them, "You see the distress in which we are, how Jerusalem lies desolate and its gates have been given to fire. Come, and let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, that we may no longer be a reproach."
verses.2:18: And I told them of the hand of God which is good upon me, and also the king's words which he had spoken to me; and I said, "Let us arise and build." And their hands were strengthened for good.
verses.2:19: And Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard of it; and they laughed us to scorn, and came upon us and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
verses.2:20: And I returned an answer to them and said to them, "The God of heaven Himself will prosper us, and we are His pure servants, and we will build; but you have no portion, nor righteousness, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
verses.3:1: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and set up its doors, and they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
verses.3:2: And next to them were the men of the sons of Jericho, and next to them the sons of Zabaur the son of Amarei.
verses.3:3: And the Fish Gate was built by the sons of Asan; they roofed it, and they roofed its doors, and its locks, and its bars.
verses.3:4: And next to them repair was made by Ramoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz. And next to them Zadok the son of Baana repaired.
verses.3:5: And next to them the Tekoites repaired, but Adoreem did not put their neck to their service.
verses.3:6: And the Gate of Isana was repaired by Joeiaa the son of Phasek and Meshullam the son of Badia; they roofed it, and set up its doors, and its locks, and its bars.
verses.3:8: And next to them Hananiah the son of Joakim made repairs, and they left Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
verses.3:9: And next to them Rephaiah, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
verses.3:10: And next to them Jedaiah the son of Heromath repaired, even opposite his own house. And next to him Hatuth the son of Hasbanam repaired.
verses.3:11: And second, Malchijah the son of Heram and Hashub the son of Phaab-moab repaired, even as far as the Tower of the Nathureim.
verses.3:12: And next to him Shallum the son of Heliah, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.
verses.3:13: The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the inhabitants of Zano; they built it, and set up its doors, and its locks, and its bars, and a thousand cubits on the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
verses.3:14: And the Dung Gate was repaired by Malchijah the son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-acham, he and his sons; and they covered it, and set up its doors, and its locks, and its bars.
verses.3:15: And the wall of the Pool of the Fleeces, by the king's shearing, and as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.
verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah the son of Azabuch, ruler of the district of Besor, repaired as far as the garden of the tomb of David, and as far as the pool that was made, and as far as Beth-abareim.
verses.3:17: After him the Levites repaired, Basuth the son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
verses.3:18: After him their brethren repaired, Bedei the son of Henadalat, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
verses.3:19: And next to him Azur the son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired a second measure of the tower of the ascent that joins the corner.
verses.3:20: After him Baruch the son of Zabu repaired a second measure, from the corner to the door of Beth-elishub the high priest.
verses.3:21: After him Meramoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakob, repaired a second measure, from the door of Beth-elishub to the end of Beth-elishub.
verses.3:22: And after him the priests, the men of Hachechar, repaired.
verses.3:23: And after him Benjamin and Hashub repaired opposite their house. After him Azariah the son of Madasel, the son of Ananiah, repaired beside his own house.
verses.3:24: After him Bani the son of Henadad repaired a second measure, from Beth-azariah to the corner and to the turning.
verses.3:25: Palal the son of Euei repaired opposite the corner, and the upper tower that projects from the king's house, which belongs to the court of the guard. And after him Pedaiah the son of Phoros.
verses.3:26: Now the Katheneim were dwelling in Ophel, as far as the garden of the Water Gate toward the east, and the projecting tower.
verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites repaired a second measure, opposite the great projecting tower, and as far as the wall of Ophel.
verses.3:28: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each man opposite his own house.
verses.3:29: After him Zadok the son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah the son of Echeniah, the keeper of the house of the east, repaired.
verses.3:30: After him Hananiah the son of Telemiah, and Hanum the sixth son of Sele, repaired a second measure. After him Meshullam the son of Berechiah repaired opposite his treasury.
verses.3:31: After him Malchijah the son of Saraphei repaired as far as Beth-anatheim, and the merchants, opposite the Gate of Maphekad, and as far as the middle of the turning.
verses.3:32: And in the midst of the ascent of the Sheep Gate, the coppersmiths and the merchants repaired.
verses.3:33: And it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that it seemed grievous to him, and he was exceedingly angry, and he mocked the Jews.
verses.3:34: And he said before his brethren, "Is this the army of Samaria, that these Jews are building their own city?"
verses.3:35: And Tobiah the Ammonite came beside him, and they said to one another, "Will they sacrifice or eat in their place? Will not a fox go up and tear down their wall of stones?"
verses.3:36: Hear, O our God, for we have become an object of derision; and turn their reproach upon their own head, and give them over to derision in a land of captivity,
verses.3:37: and do not cover over iniquity.
verses.4:1: And it came to pass, when Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabs and the Ammonites heard that the growth had risen upon the walls of Jerusalem, that the breaches had begun to be closed up, it appeared exceedingly evil to them.
verses.4:2: And all of them gathered together as one to come and wage war in Jerusalem.
verses.4:3: And we prayed to our God, and set guards against them day and night because of them.
verses.4:4: And Judah said, "The strength of the enemies is crushed, and there is a great multitude, and we shall not be able to build on the wall."
verses.4:5: And those who afflicted us said, "They will not know and will not see until we come into their midst and slay them and bring the work to an end."
verses.4:6: And it came to pass, when the Jews who dwelt near them came, they said to us, "They are coming up from all the places against us."
verses.4:7: And I stationed men in the lowest parts of the place behind the wall, in the sheltered places, and I stationed the people by clans with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
verses.4:8: And I looked, and arose and spoke to the nobles and to the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid before them; remember our great and awesome God, and contend in battle for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses."
verses.4:9: And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it had become known to us, that God thwarted their counsel; and all of us returned to the wall, each man to his own work.
verses.4:10: And it came to pass from that day onward that half of those who had been shaken out were doing the work, while half of them held fast—and there were spears and shields and the bows and the breastplates, and the rulers were behind the whole house of Judah,
verses.4:11: who were building on the wall. And those who bore burdens with carrying-straps were under arms: with one hand a man did the work itself, and with one he grasped the javelin.
verses.4:12: And as for the builders, each man had his sword girded upon his loins as they were building; and the one who sounded the horn stood beside him.
verses.4:13: And I said to the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, "The work is broad and great, and we are scattered upon the wall, each man far from his brother.
verses.4:14: In whatever place you hear the sound of the horn, there you shall gather to us, and our God will fight for us."
verses.4:15: So we were doing the work, while half of them held the spears from the rising up until the dawn, until the coming forth of the stars.
verses.4:16: And at that time I said to the people, "Lodge in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be a guard for you, and the day for work."
verses.4:17: So I remained, along with the men of the guard behind me, and not a man among us took off his garments.
verses.5:1: Now there was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brethren the Jews.
verses.5:2: And there were some who said, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many; and we shall obtain grain, and we shall eat and live."
verses.5:3: And there are some who say, "Our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses we are pledging as security; and we shall obtain grain and eat."
verses.5:4: And there are some who say, "We have borrowed silver for the tribute of the king—our fields, and our vineyards, and our houses.
verses.5:5: Now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, and their sons are as our sons; yet behold, we are forcing our sons and our daughters into bondage, and some of our daughters are already held in bondage; and there is no power in our hand, and our fields and our vineyards belong to the nobles."
verses.5:6: And I was exceedingly grieved when I heard their outcry and these words.
verses.5:7: And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended with the nobles and the rulers, and said to them, "With exactions you are demanding payment, each man from his brother." And I convened a great assembly against them,
verses.5:8: and I said to them, "We have purchased our brethren the Jews who were sold to the nations, of our own free will; and do you sell our brethren?" And they kept silent and found no word.
verses.5:9: And I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good; not in this way, in the fear of our God, shall you depart from the reproach of our enemies.
verses.5:10: And my brethren and my acquaintances and I have lent them silver and grain, yet we have relinquished this exaction.
verses.5:11: Restore now yourselves, even today, their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses; and from the silver, the grain and the wine, and bring them forth for yourselves."
verses.5:12: And they said, "We will restore them, and from them we will seek nothing; thus we will do, just as you say." Then I summoned the priests and made them swear an oath to do according to this word.
verses.5:13: And I shook out my mantle and said, "So may God shake out every man who does not uphold this word from his house and from his labor, and so he shall be shaken out and empty." And all the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the Lord; and the people did according to this word.
verses.5:14: From the day on which he commanded me to be their ruler in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Arsenatha—twelve years—I and our brethren did not eat of their forced exaction.
verses.5:15: And as for the former exactions which they laid heavily upon them before me, they also took from them in bread and in wine the last silver, forty didrachmas, and their shaken-out ones exercise authority over the people; yet I did not do so because of the fear of God.
verses.5:16: And in the work of the wall of these people I did not take hold, and a field I did not acquire; and all those who were gathered were there for the work.
verses.5:17: And the Jews, one hundred and fifty men, as well as those coming to us from the nations around us, were at my table.
verses.5:18: Now that which was prepared for one day was one calf, and choice sheep and a young goat were prepared for me, and every ten days wine among all in abundance; yet with all this I did not seek the bread of forced exaction, because the servitude was heavy upon this people.
verses.5:19: Remember me, O God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.
verses.6:1: And it came to pass, when it was heard by Sanballat and Tobiah, and by Geshem the Arab, and by the rest of our enemies, that the wall had been built, and that no breath was left in them—up to that time I had not set up doors in the gates—
verses.6:2: that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, and let us gather together in the villages in the plain of Ono." Yet they were plotting to do evil to me.
verses.6:3: And I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work, and I shall not be able to come down, lest the work cease; as soon as I have completed it, I will come down to you."
verses.6:4: And they sent to me according to this same word, and I sent back to them in the same manner.
verses.6:5: And Sanballat sent his servant to me, with an open letter in his hand.
verses.6:6: And it was written in it: "It has been heard among the nations that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; therefore you are building the wall, and you shall be king for them.
verses.6:7: And in addition to these things you have appointed prophets for yourself, so that you may sit in Jerusalem as king over Judah; and now these words will be reported to the king. Come now, therefore, and let us take counsel together."
verses.6:8: And I sent to him, saying, "Nothing has happened like these words which you speak, for out of your own heart you are fabricating them."
verses.6:9: For all of them are seeking to frighten us, saying, "Their hands will grow weak from this work, and it will not be done." And now I strengthened my hands.
verses.6:10: And I entered the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah, the son of Meitael, who was shut in; and he said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, in its midst, and let us shut its doors, for they are coming by night to slay you."
verses.6:11: And I said, "Who is the man who will enter into the house and live?"
verses.6:12: And I perceived, and behold, God had not sent him, for the prophecy was a word against me; and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired
verses.6:13: a multitude against me, in order that I might be afraid and act thus and sin, and become for them an evil name, so that they might reproach me.
verses.6:14: Remember, O God, Tobiah and Anaballat according to these his deeds, and also Noadiah the prophet and the rest of the priests who were frightening me.
verses.6:15: So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of Edud, in fifty-two days.
verses.6:16: And it came to pass, when our enemies heard of it, that all the nations around us were afraid, and exceeding fear fell in their own eyes; and they knew that it was from our God that this work had been brought to completion.
verses.6:17: Moreover, in those days letters were going forth from many nobles of Judah to Tobiah, and those of Tobiah were coming to them;
verses.6:18: for many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah, and Johanan his son had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah as his wife.
verses.6:19: And they were speaking his words before me, and they were carrying out my words to him; and Tobiah sent letters to frighten me.
verses.7:1: Now it came to pass, when the wall was built and I had set up the doors, that the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
verses.7:2: And I gave charge to Hananiah my brother, and to Hananiah the ruler of the citadel in Jerusalem, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many.
verses.7:3: And I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun is up; and while they are still keeping watch, let the doors be shut and barred; and appoint guards from those who dwell in Jerusalem, each man at his watch, and each man opposite his own house."
verses.7:4: Now the city was broad and great, yet the people within it were few, and houses had not been built.
verses.7:5: Then God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the rulers, and the people into companies; and I found a book of the company of those who had come up at the first, and found written in it:
verses.7:6: And these are the sons of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away into exile, and who returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each man to his own city,
verses.7:7: with Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and Nehemiah, Azariah, Naamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Maspheran, Ezra, Batoi, Nahum, Baanah, and Masphar. The men of the son of Israel:
verses.7:8: The sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
verses.7:9: The sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
verses.7:10: The sons of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two;
verses.7:11: The sons of Pahath-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Jobab, two thousand eight hundred and eighteen;
verses.7:12: The sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
verses.7:13: The sons of Zathuia, eight hundred and forty;
verses.7:14: The sons of Zathu, eight hundred and sixty;
verses.7:15: The sons of Binnui, six hundred and forty-eight;
verses.7:16: The sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-eight;
verses.7:17: The sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-eight;
verses.7:18: The sons of Adikam, six hundred and sixty-seven;
verses.7:19: The sons of Batoi, two thousand and sixty-seven;
verses.7:20: The sons of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five;
verses.7:21: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
verses.7:22: The sons of Hashum, three hundred and twenty-eight;
verses.7:23: The sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-four;
verses.7:24: The sons of Hariph, one hundred and twelve;
verses.7:26: The sons of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three; the sons of Atopha, fifty-six;
verses.7:27: The sons of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
verses.7:29: The men of Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and twenty-one;
verses.7:30: The men of Ramah and Tamal, six hundred and twenty-one;
verses.7:31: The men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;
verses.7:32: The men of Bethel and Halia, one hundred and twenty-three;
verses.7:34: The men of Elam-Aar, one thousand two hundred and fifty;
verses.7:35: The sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
verses.7:36: The sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
verses.7:37: The sons of Lod, Hadia, and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-one;
verses.7:38: The sons of Sananat, nine hundred and thirty.
verses.7:39: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
verses.7:40: The sons, one thousand and fifty-two;
verses.7:41: The sons of Phasedur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
verses.7:42: The sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
verses.7:43: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kabdiel, of the sons of Thuduia, seventy-four;
verses.7:44: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight;
verses.7:45: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater the son of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Aku, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, one hundred and thirty-eight.
verses.7:46: The Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Gabaoth,
verses.7:47: the sons of Kira, the sons of Asuia, the sons of Padon,
verses.7:48: the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai,
verses.7:49: the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:50: the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,
verses.7:51: the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzzi, the sons of Paseah,
verses.7:52: the sons of Besai, the sons of Mesinom, the sons of Nephishesim,
verses.7:53: the sons of Bakbu, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harum,
verses.7:54: the sons of Basaoth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Hadasan,
verses.7:55: the sons of Barkue, the sons of Sedirath, the sons of Hemath,
verses.7:56: the sons of Asia, the sons of Hatipha.
verses.7:57: The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
verses.7:58: the sons of Jelel, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:59: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hegel, the sons of Pochereth, the sons of Zebaim, the sons of Emim.
verses.7:60: All the Nethinim and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
verses.7:61: And these came up from Tel-Meleth, Haresa, Cherub, Heron, and Immer; yet they could not declare their fathers' houses and their seed, whether they were of Israel:
verses.7:62: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two.
verses.7:63: And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, because he took wives from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called by their name.
verses.7:64: These sought their written record of the company, and it was not found; and they were removed from the priesthood.
verses.7:65: And Hasersatha said that they should not eat of the most holy things until the priest should arise to give light.
verses.7:66: And the whole assembly was about forty-two thousand three hundred and eight,
verses.7:67: besides their male servants and their female servants, who were three hundred and thirty-seven; and singing men and singing women, two hundred and forty-five;
verses.7:70: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave for the work to Nehemiah for the treasury: one thousand gold pieces, fifty basins, and thirty mechonoth of the priests.
verses.7:71: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses put into the treasury of the year twenty thousand pieces of gold, and two thousand two hundred minas of silver,
verses.7:72: and sixty-seven mechonoth of the priests.
verses.7:73: And the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, those from among the people, the Nethinim, and all Israel settled in their cities.
verses.8:1: And when the seventh month arrived, while the children of Israel were in their cities, all the people assembled as a single man in the broad square before the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which He had commanded Israel.
verses.8:2: So Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation, from man to woman and everyone able to comprehend what was heard, on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And he read from it from the hour of the sun's breaking forth until midday in the presence of the men and the women, and they understood; and the ears of all the people were turned toward the book of the law.
verses.8:4: Now Ezra the scribe stood upon a wooden platform, and he stationed next to him Mattathias, Shemaiah, Ananiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, and Zechariah.
verses.8:5: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, because he stood higher than the people; and it came to pass that when he opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.8:6: And he blessed the Lord, the great God; and all the people answered and declared, "Amen," and they bowed low and worshiped the Lord with their faces to the earth.
verses.8:7: And Jeshua, Benaiah, and Sherebiah were instructing the people in the law, while the people remained in their station.
verses.8:8: So they read from the book of the law of God, and Ezra taught and expounded in the knowledge of the Lord, and the people grasped the meaning of the reading.
verses.8:9: Then Nehemiah spoke, while Ezra the priest and scribe and the Levites were instructing the people, and they declared to all the people, "This day is holy to the Lord our God; do not mourn nor weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.
verses.8:10: And he said to them, "Go forth, eat rich foods and drink sweet beverages, and send a portion to those who have nothing, for this day is holy to our Lord; and do not falter, for He is our strength."
verses.8:11: Likewise the Levites quieted the people, saying, "Be still, for the day is holy, and do not be downcast."
verses.8:12: So all the people departed to eat and drink, to dispatch portions, and to celebrate with exceeding gladness, because they understood the words which he had made known to them.
verses.8:13: And on the second day the chiefs of the ancestral houses gathered together with all the people, the priests, and the Levites to Ezra the scribe, in order to give careful heed to all the words of the law.
verses.8:14: And they discovered written in the law which the Lord had commanded Moses that the children of Israel should dwell in booths during the feast in the seventh month,
verses.8:15: and that they should sound trumpets throughout all their cities and in Jerusalem. Therefore Ezra said, "Go out to the mountain and gather leaves of olive, and leaves of cypress wood, and leaves of myrtle, and leaves of palms, and leaves of thick-leaved trees, to build booths according to what is written."
verses.8:16: So the people went out and brought them, and constructed booths for themselves, each man upon his own rooftop, and in their courtyards, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the broad squares of the city, even as far as the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.8:17: Thus the entire congregation of those who had returned from captivity constructed booths and dwelt in booths; for from the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day the children of Israel had not done so. And there was great gladness.
verses.8:18: And he read from the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day until the final day; and they kept the feast seven days, and on the eighth day held a closing solemnity.
verses.9:1: And on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel assembled with fasting and clad in sackcloth.
verses.9:2: And the children of Israel separated themselves from every child of a foreigner, and they stood and confessed their own sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
verses.9:3: They stood in their appointed place and read from the book of the law of their God; and they were confessing to the Lord and worshiping their God.
verses.9:4: Then Jeshua and the sons of Kadmiel, and Sherebiah the son of Arabiah, stood upon the raised steps of the Levites, and they cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
verses.9:5: And the Levites Jeshua and Kadmiel said, "Arise, bless the Lord our God from everlasting even to everlasting; and they shall bless the name of Your glory, and shall exalt it above all blessing and praise."
verses.9:6: And Ezra said, "You Yourself alone are the Lord; You fashioned the heaven of heaven and all their array, the earth and everything that exists upon it, the seas and everything within them, and You give life to all things; and the armies of the heavens bow down in worship to You.
verses.9:7: You are God; You chose Abram and brought him out from the land of the Chaldeans, and conferred upon him the name Abraham.
verses.9:8: You found his heart faithful before You, and established a covenant with him to grant to him and to his seed the territory of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites; and You fulfilled Your words, because You are righteous.
verses.9:9: You beheld the humiliation of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their outcry beside the Red Sea.
verses.9:10: You displayed signs and wonders in Egypt, upon Pharaoh and upon all his servants and upon all the populace of his land, for You knew that they acted arrogantly against them; and You made a name for Yourself, even as on this day.
verses.9:11: You tore open the sea before him, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground; and those who pursued them You hurled into the depths, like a stone into raging water.
verses.9:12: With a pillar of cloud You guided them by day, and with a pillar of fire through the night, to illuminate for them the pathway along which they should travel.
verses.9:13: Upon Mount Sinai You descended and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them upright judgments and laws of truth, good ordinances and commandments.
verses.9:14: Your holy Sabbath You made known to them, and commandments, ordinances, and law You enjoined upon them through the hand of Moses Your servant.
verses.9:15: Bread out of heaven You provided them for their sustenance, and water out of a rock You brought forth to them for their thirst; and You told them to enter in and inherit the land over which You had stretched out Your hand to grant it to them.
verses.9:16: Yet they stiffened their neck, and did not heed Your commandments.
verses.9:17: They refused to listen, and did not remember Your wondrous works which You had wrought among them; rather, they hardened their neck, and appointed a ruler to return to their bondage in Egypt. Yet You are a merciful and compassionate God, longsuffering and abounding in mercy, and You did not forsake them.
verses.9:18: Furthermore, they even forged for themselves a molten calf and declared, 'These are the gods who led us out of Egypt,' and they committed great provocations.
verses.9:19: Yet You, in Your abundant compassions, did not abandon them in the wilderness; You did not turn aside the pillar of cloud from them by day to guide them along the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to illumine for them the path in which they should walk.
verses.9:20: Your good Spirit You bestowed to instruct them, and Your manna You did not withhold from their mouth, and water You supplied them for their thirst.
verses.9:21: For forty years You nourished them in the wilderness; You did not fail them; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not crack open.
verses.9:22: You handed over to them kings and peoples, and apportioned them out to them; and they inherited the territory of Sihon and that of Og, king of Bashan.
verses.9:23: Their children You multiplied like the stars of heaven, and led them into the land of which You had spoken to their fathers, and they inherited it.
verses.9:24: You utterly crushed before them the inhabitants of the land of the Canaanites, and delivered them into their hands—both their kings and the peoples of the land—to deal with them as was pleasing in their sight.
verses.9:25: And they seized lofty cities, and came into possession of houses filled with all manner of good things, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive groves, and every fruit-bearing tree in abundance; so they ate and were filled and grew sleek, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness.
verses.9:26: Yet they raised a defiant cry and turned away from You, and flung Your law behind their body, and slew Your prophets who bore solemn witness against them to bring them back to You; and they committed great provocations.
verses.9:27: Therefore You handed them over into the hand of those who afflicted them, and they afflicted them; yet they cried aloud to You in the season of their distress, and from Your heaven You heard, and in Your great compassions You gave them saviors and delivered them out of the hand of him who afflicted them.
verses.9:28: Yet once they had rest, they turned back to practicing evil in Your sight; so You left them in the hands of their adversaries, who held dominion over them. Then again they cried aloud to You, and from heaven You listened and rescued them in Your manifold compassions,
verses.9:29: and You solemnly warned them to bring them back to Your law; yet they would not listen, but sinned against Your commandments and in Your judgments—which, if a man performs them, he shall live by them—and they presented a stubborn back and stiffened their neck, and refused to listen.
verses.9:30: Still You bore patiently with them for many years, and testified against them by Your Spirit through the ministry of Your prophets; yet they would not incline their ears, so You gave them over into the hand of the peoples of the land.
verses.9:31: Nevertheless, in Your abundant compassions You did not bring complete destruction upon them, nor did You forsake them, for You are mighty, merciful, and compassionate.
verses.9:32: And now, O our God—the mighty, the great, the powerful, and the awesome One, who keeps Your covenant and Your mercy—do not let all the hardship seem small before You that has overtaken us, our kings, our rulers, our priests, our prophets, our fathers, and all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria even until this present day.
verses.9:33: Yet You are righteous concerning all things that have come upon us, because You have acted in truth, whereas we have sinned grievously,
verses.9:34: and our kings, our rulers, our priests, and our fathers did not carry out Your law, nor did they pay heed to Your commandments and Your testimonies with which You solemnly warned them.
verses.9:35: Even in Your kingdom, and amid Your abundant goodness which You bestowed upon them, and in the spacious and fertile land which You set before them, they did not serve You, nor did they turn away from their wicked practices.
verses.9:36: Behold, today we are bondservants; and the land which You granted to our fathers to eat its fruit
verses.9:37: is given to the kings whom You have placed over us on account of our sins; and they exercise dominion over our bodies and over our livestock according to their pleasure, and we are in great distress."
verses.10:1: And in all these things we make a faithful covenant and write it; and our rulers, our Levites, and our priests set their seal to it.
verses.10:2: Now over those who sealed were Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah, and Zedekiah
verses.10:3: the son of Seraiah, and Azariah, and Jeremiah,
verses.10:9: Nadeiah, Belseiah, Shemaiah—these were the priests.
verses.10:10: And the Levites: Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadab, Kadmiel,
verses.10:11: and his brethren: Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kanta,
verses.10:15: The rulers of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, the sons of Bani,
verses.10:16: the sons of Bani, Azgad, Bebai,
verses.10:29: Now the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and everyone who came from the peoples of the land to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who knew and understood—
verses.10:30: prevailed over their brethren, laid a curse upon them, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all our commandments and His judgments,
verses.10:31: and not to give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and their daughters we will not take for our sons;
verses.10:32: and as for the peoples of the land who bring wares and every kind of merchandise on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and we will forego the seventh year and the exaction of every hand.
verses.10:33: And we will lay commandments upon ourselves, to charge ourselves to give a third of a didrachma every year for the service of the house of our God:
verses.10:34: for the loaves of the Presence and the continual offering, and for the continual burnt offering of the Sabbaths, of the New Moons, for the feasts and for the holy things, and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for the works of the house of our God.
verses.10:35: And we cast lots concerning the lot of the wood offering—the priests, the Levites, and the people—to bring it into the house of our God, by the house of our fathers, at appointed seasons year by year, to burn upon the altar of our God, as it is written in the book;
verses.10:36: and to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of the fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house,
verses.10:37: and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring them into the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
verses.10:38: And the firstfruits of our grain and the fruit of every tree, of wine and of oil, we will bring to the priests, to the treasury of the house of God, and the tithe of our land to the Levites; and the Levites themselves shall collect the tithes in all the cities of our labor.
verses.10:39: And the priest, Aaron, shall be with the Levite in the tithe of the Levite, and the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithe into the house of our God, to the treasuries, to the house of God.
verses.10:40: For the children of Israel and the Levites shall bring the firstfruits of the grain, of the wine, and of the oil into the storehouses; and there are the holy vessels, and the priests, and the ministers, and the gatekeepers, and the singers; and we will not forsake the house of our God.
verses.11:1: Now the rulers of the people dwelt in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people drew lots to bring one out of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine parts in the cities.
verses.11:2: And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.11:3: Now these are the rulers of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem; and in the cities of Judah each man dwelt in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the sons of the servants of Solomon.
verses.11:4: And in Jerusalem there dwelt some of the sons of Judah and of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah the son of Azed, the son of Zechariah, the son of Samareiah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Malelem, and of the sons of Perez;
verses.11:5: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Chalea, the son of Hoziah, the son of Dalea, the son of Joiarib, the son of Thezeiah, the son of Delone.
verses.11:6: All the sons of Seres who dwelt in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight men of valor.
verses.11:7: And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Amesula, Joed the son of Phalaiah, the son of Kodaiah, the son of Magael, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah;
verses.11:8: and after him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.
verses.11:9: And Joel the son of Zichri was overseer over them, and Judah the son of Hasana was second over the city.
verses.11:10: Of the priests also: Dadeiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,
verses.11:11: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Apoboch, opposite the house of God.
verses.11:12: And their brethren who did the work of the house: Amzi the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah,
verses.11:13: rulers of fathers' houses, two hundred and forty-two. And Amaseiah the son of Esdriel,
verses.11:14: and his brethren, mighty men of battle, one hundred and twenty-eight; and the overseer was Badiel.
verses.11:15: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Ezerei;
verses.11:17: and Mattaniah the son of Mica, and Obeb the son of Shammua,
verses.11:19: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren, one hundred and seventy-two.
verses.11:22: And the overseer of the Levites was the son of Bani, Uzzi the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, opposite the work of the house of God.
verses.11:23: For there was a commandment of the king concerning them.
verses.11:24: And Pethahiah the son of Baseza was at the king's hand in every matter for the people.
verses.11:25: And concerning the villages in their field: some of the sons of Judah dwelt in Kiriathar,
verses.11:30: and their villages, Lachish and its fields; and they encamped in Beersheba.
verses.11:31: And the sons of Benjamin were from Gala, Michmash.
verses.11:36: And of the Levites, divisions of Judah were for Benjamin.
verses.12:1: Now these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
verses.12:7: These were the chiefs of the priests and their brethren in the days of Jeshua.
verses.12:8: And the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Machaniah; he and his brethren were over the hands for the divisions.
verses.12:10: And Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib, Joiada,
verses.12:11: and Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
verses.12:12: And in the days of Joiakim, his brethren, the priests and the chiefs of the fathers' houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah,
verses.12:13: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Johanan;
verses.12:14: of Malluch, Jonathan; of Shecaniah, Joseph;
verses.12:15: of Are, Mannas; of Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.12:16: of Adadai, Zechariah; of Ganathoth, Meshullam;
verses.12:17: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miamin, Maadai; of Piltai;
verses.12:19: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jonathan; of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Edio, Uzzi;
verses.12:20: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Abed;
verses.12:21: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Isdeiu, Nethanel.
verses.12:22: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Joa, and Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as chiefs of the fathers' houses, and the priests during the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.12:23: The sons of Levi, the chiefs of the fathers' houses, were written in the book of the chronicles of the days, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.
verses.12:24: And the chiefs of the Levites were Habiah and Sherebiah and Jeshua, and the sons of Kadmiel and their brethren opposite them, to sing hymns and to give praise, according to the commandment of David the man of God, division opposite division,
verses.12:26: in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, in the days of Nehemiah, and Ezra the priest, the scribe.
verses.12:27: Now at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites in their places to bring them to Jerusalem, to hold a dedication and rejoicing with thanksgivings and with songs, playing cymbals and harps.
verses.12:28: And the sons of the singers gathered together both from the surrounding region all around Jerusalem and from the villages,
verses.12:29: and from the fields; for the singers had built villages for themselves in Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gatekeepers and the wall.
verses.12:31: And they brought the leaders of Judah up upon the wall.
verses.12:32: And Hoshaiah went after them, with half of the leaders of Judah,
verses.12:34: Judah, and Benjamin, and Seraiah, and Jeremiah;
verses.12:35: and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Johanan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Nathaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
verses.12:36: and his brethren, Shemaiah and Uzziel, to give praise with the songs of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was before him.
verses.12:37: At the Gate of Praise opposite them, they went up by the stairs of the cities of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, and as far as the Water Gate
verses.12:39: of Ephraim, and to the Fish Gate, and by the Tower of Hananel, and as far as the Sheep Gate.
verses.12:42: And the singers were heard, and they were overseen.
verses.12:43: And on that day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice greatly; and their wives and their children rejoiced, and the rejoicing in Jerusalem was heard from afar.
verses.12:44: And on that day they appointed men over the storerooms, for the treasuries, for the firstfruits, and for the tithes, and for the leaders of the cities gathered in them, portions for the priests and for the Levites; for there was rejoicing in Judah over the priests and over the Levites who stood.
verses.12:45: And they kept the charges of their God and the charges of purification, and the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commandments of David and of Solomon his son.
verses.12:46: For in the days of David, Asaph from the beginning was chief of the singers, and of the hymn and praise to God.
verses.12:47: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel gave the portions of the singers and of the gatekeepers, each day's share in its day, and consecrated them for the Levites, and the Levites consecrated them for the sons of Aaron.
verses.13:1: On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the hearing of the people; and it was found written in it that Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the assembly of God forever,
verses.13:2: because they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and with water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse; yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.
verses.13:3: And it came to pass, when they heard the law, that all the mixed multitude in Israel were separated.
verses.13:4: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who dwelt in the storeroom of the house of our God, was closely related to Tobiah.
verses.13:5: And he made for himself a great storeroom, where formerly they had put the grain offering, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the grain and of the wine and of the oil, the commanded portion of the Levites and of the singers and of the gatekeepers, and the firstfruits of the priests.
verses.13:6: And during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king; and after the end of some days I asked leave of the king,
verses.13:7: and I came to Jerusalem; and I perceived the evil, in making for him a storeroom in the court of the house of God.
verses.13:8: And it seemed exceedingly evil to me, and I cast all the furnishings of the house of Tobiah out of the storeroom;
verses.13:9: and I gave command, and I purified the storerooms, and I returned there the vessels of the house of God, the manna and the frankincense.
verses.13:10: And I came to know that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and that the Levites and the singers who performed the work had fled, each man to his own field.
verses.13:11: And I contended and said, "Why has the house of God been forsaken?" And I gathered them together, and they stationed them at their post.
verses.13:12: And all Judah brought the tithe of the wheat and of the wine and of the oil into the treasuries,
verses.13:13: into the hand of Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah of the Levites; and under their hand was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Nathaniah, for they were reckoned faithful, and it rested upon them to distribute to their brethren.
verses.13:14: Remember me, O God, in this, and may my mercy not be blotted out, which I have shown in the house of the Lord God.
verses.13:15: In those days I saw in Judah some treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and loading upon the donkeys both wine and grapes and figs and every kind of burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day; and I testified on the day of their selling.
verses.13:16: And they dwelt in it, bringing fish and all manner of merchandise, selling on the Sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.13:17: And I contended with the freeborn sons of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you do, and profane the Sabbath day?
verses.13:18: Did not your fathers do thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us all these evils, and upon this city? And do you add wrath upon Israel, to profane the Sabbath?"
verses.13:19: And it came to pass, when the gates of Jerusalem were set in place before the Sabbath, that I shut the gates, and I gave word that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath; and I stationed some at the gates, that no burdens should be carried on the Sabbath day.
verses.13:20: And all of them lodged and carried on trade outside Jerusalem once and twice.
verses.13:21: And I testified against them and said to them, "Why do you lodge opposite the wall? If you do so a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you." From that time they did not come on the Sabbath.
verses.13:22: And I spoke to the Levites, who were purifying themselves and coming to guard the gates, sanctifying the Sabbath day. Concerning these things remember me, O God, and spare me according to the multitude of Your mercy.
verses.13:23: And in those days I saw the Jews who had taken Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite women to dwell with them,
verses.13:24: and half of their children spoke in the tongue of Ashdod, and they did not know how to speak in the tongue of Judah.
verses.13:25: And I contended with them and cursed them, and struck some of the men among them, and made them swear by God, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons.
verses.13:26: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin in this very way? Yet among many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet even him foreign women caused to turn aside.
verses.13:27: And shall we listen to you to do all this wickedness, to break faith with our God by taking foreign women to dwell with you?"
verses.13:28: And one of the sons of Joiada the son of Eliashib the high priest was a son-in-law of Sanballat; and I cast them out from me.
verses.13:29: Remember them, O God, concerning the kinship of the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood, and the Levites.
verses.13:30: And I purified them from all that was foreign, and I established divisions for the priests and for the Levites, each man according to his work,
verses.13:31: and the offering of the wood-bearers at seasons from time to time, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O our God, for good.

notes.1:1: Greek reads Helkiah (for Hebrew Hacaliah), the month Secheelu (for Chislev), and transliterates Hebrew habbirah ("the citadel") as Abira.
notes.1:5: The Greek phrase me de (literally "not indeed," also in 1:11) is a Septuagint idiom rendering the Hebrew particle of entreaty ("Ah, I pray").
notes.1:11: The Greek text reads eunouchos ("eunuch") rather than oinochoos ("cupbearer").
notes.2:1: The Greek text reads "before me" and "there was no other before him," differing from the Hebrew ("before him" and "I had not been sad in his presence").
notes.2:6: Greek pallake literally means "concubine," rendering the Hebrew term for a royal consort.
notes.2:13: Greek transliterates the Valley Gate as "Golela," renders the spring as "the Spring of the Figs," and uses syntribon ("breaking/shattering," also in 2:15) where the Hebrew root means "inspecting."
notes.2:20: Greek reads katharoi ("pure/clean"), whereas the Hebrew reads "we will arise."
notes.3:5: Greek leaves the Hebrew word for "their nobles" untranslated as Adoreem; similarly, Greek transliterates several place and group names in this chapter (Isana in 3:6, Nathureim in 3:11, Hachechar in 3:22, and Katheneim in 3:26).
notes.3:15: The Greek text omits the first part of the verse and renders the Hebrew "Pool of Shelah by the king's garden" as "the Pool of the Fleeces, by the king's shearing."
notes.3:34: Greek places "the army of Samaria" inside Sanballat's taunt rather than as part of his audience, and presents a shorter speech than the Hebrew (verses 3:33-37 correspond to 4:1-5 in most English Bibles).
notes.4:1: The Greek reads "the growth had risen" (φυή, denoting advancing restoration) and "it appeared exceedingly evil to them" rather than "they became very angry," and does not mention the Ashdodites.
notes.4:4: The Greek reads "the strength of the enemies is crushed, and there is a great multitude," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "the strength of the burden-bearers is failing, and there is much rubble."
notes.4:7: The Greek specifies "in the sheltered places" (ἐν τοῖς σκεπεινοῖς), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to open or exposed places.
notes.4:10: The Greek phrase "those who had been shaken out" (τῶν ἐκτετιναγμένων) renders the Hebrew for "young men/servants" by associating it with the Hebrew verb meaning "to shake out"; the same rendering recurs in 5:15.
notes.5:6: The Greek reads "I was exceedingly grieved" (ἐλυπήθην σφόδρα), expressing deep sorrow rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "I became very angry."
notes.5:11: The Greek reads "from the silver, the grain and the wine, and bring them forth for yourselves," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's call to return the hundredth part of the silver, grain, wine, and oil.
notes.5:14: The Greek preserves the distinct royal name "Arsenatha" (Ἀρσεναθά) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Artaxerxes," and renders the governor's allowance with βία ("forced exaction"), a rendering continued in 5:15 and 5:18.
notes.5:15: The Greek reads "the last silver, forty didrachmas" (double drachmas rather than shekels) and again uses "their shaken-out ones" (οἱ ἐκτετιναγμένοι; compare 4:10).
notes.5:16: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("I held fast to the work on this wall"), the Greek contains a negation ("I did not take hold") and refers to "all those who were gathered" rather than Nehemiah's servants.
notes.6:1: The Greek reads "no breath was left in them" (πνοή) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "no breach was left in it."
notes.6:3: Rather than asking rhetorically why the work should stop while he leaves it, the Greek has Nehemiah warn against the work ceasing and add, "as soon as I have completed it, I will come down to you."
notes.6:10: The Greek gives the grandfather's name as "Meitael" (Μειταήλ) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Mehetabel."
notes.6:14: The Greek reads "Anaballat" (Ἀναβαλλάτ, lacking the initial sigma of Sanballat), gives Noadiah the masculine title "the prophet" (τῷ προφήτῃ) rather than "prophetess," and refers to "the rest of the priests" instead of "the rest of the prophets."
notes.6:15: The Greek gives the month name as "Edud" (Ἐδούδ) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Elul."
notes.7:2: The Greek text names both Nehemiah's brother and the ruler of the citadel "Hananiah" (where the Hebrew text distinguishes "Hanani" and "Hananiah"); "citadel" translates the Greek loanword beira.
notes.7:3: "Until the sun is up" translates the Greek phrase meaning literally "until together with the sun," where the Hebrew text reads "until the sun is hot."
notes.7:5: Greek synodia ("company" or "caravan") stands here where the Hebrew text refers to enrollment by genealogy.
notes.7:7: The Greek list includes Ezra and treats Hebrew mispar ("the number of") as a personal name, Masphar, while also reading Naamiah, Maspheran, and Batoi, and concluding with "the men of the son of Israel" where the Hebrew has "the men of the people of Israel."
notes.7:33: In verses 33–34, the Greek text transliterates the Hebrew word for "other" as aar ("Nabia-Aar" and "Elam-Aar"); throughout this register, the translation likewise preserves distinct Greek names and totals (such as Jobab in 7:11; Zathuia and Zathu in 7:13–14; Atopha with separate totals in 7:26; Tamal in 7:30; Halia in 7:32; and 1,250 in 7:34).
notes.7:40: The Greek text omits the priestly family name here ("Immer" in the Hebrew text), reading simply "The sons, one thousand and fifty-two." In 7:41, the Greek alphabetic numeral represents one thousand two hundred, yielding one thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
notes.7:64: The Greek passive verb (literally "were treated as next-of-kin" away from the priesthood) reflects reading the Hebrew root for "excluded as defiled" as its homonym meaning "to act as kinsman-redeemer."
notes.7:65: Hasersatha transliterates the Persian title for governor ("the Tirshatha"); "to give light" renders the Greek future participle photison, translating Hebrew "Urim" by its sense of "light" without mentioning "Thummim."
notes.7:66: In verses 66–69, the Greek text preserves shorter totals and omits verse 68 (reading 42,308 for the assembly, 337 for the servants, and 2,700 donkeys, where the Hebrew text has 42,360; 7,337; and lists horses, mules, camels, and 6,720 donkeys).
notes.7:70: In verses 70–72, Greek mechonoth transliterates a Hebrew word for "stands" or "bases" where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "priests' garments"; the Greek text also reads "to Nehemiah" (7:70), "of the year" rather than "of the work" (7:71), and a shorter text in 7:72.
notes.8:1: The Septuagint does not name "the Lord" explicitly as the subject of "commanded," leaving the clause simply "which He commanded Israel" (or "which he commanded Israel," referring to Moses).
notes.8:4: The Septuagint uses an active verb ("he stationed") and lists fewer men standing beside Ezra (six on his right and four on his left) than the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:8: Distinctively, the Septuagint names Ezra as teaching and expounding "in the knowledge of the Lord" during the public reading.
notes.8:10: Where the Hebrew text reads "the joy of the Lord is your strength," the Septuagint reads concisely "for He is our strength" (or "for it is our strength").
notes.8:15: The Septuagint specifies sounding trumpets across the cities and explicitly identifies Ezra as the speaker commanding the people to gather branches.
notes.9:4: The Septuagint preserves a shorter and distinct list of Levites on the platform: "Jeshua and the sons of Kadmiel, and Sherebiah the son of Arabiah."
notes.9:6: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Septuagint explicitly introduces the great penitential prayer of verses 6–37 with "And Ezra said."
notes.9:11: The Greek reads the singular pronoun "before him" (treating Israel collectively as a single nation) before continuing with plural verbs and pronouns.
notes.9:26: The Septuagint translates the rebellion literally with "raised a defiant cry" (Greek elalaxan) and "flung Your law behind their body."
notes.9:36: The Septuagint omits the final clause of verse 36 and the opening phrase of verse 37 found in the Hebrew text, connecting "the land" directly to "the kings" across the verse division.
notes.10:2: The Greek text omits the title "the governor" after Nehemiah and connects Zedekiah directly to the next verse as "the son of Seraiah," rather than listing Seraiah separately as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:7: The Greek reads "Tnathoth" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Ginnethon"; similar Septuagint-distinct forms appear across this list (including Nadeiah, Belseiah, Kanta, Hodum, the sons of Benjamin, Aiah, Phadaeis, Ara, and Enam).
notes.10:30: The Greek reads "prevailed over their brethren, laid a curse upon them" (reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew term for "their nobles") and "all our commandments and His judgments," omitting "of the Lord our Lord" and "His statutes."
notes.10:33: The Greek specifies "a third of a didrachma," using a Greek silver coin denomination where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies a third of a shekel.
notes.10:39: The Greek literally reads "the priest, Aaron" (without "the son of") and concludes with "to the house of God" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "to the storehouse."
notes.11:5: The Greek divides and renders several ancestral names differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including Chalea, Hoziah, Dalea, Thezeiah, and Delone (as well as Azed, Samareiah, Malelem, and Seres in verses 4 and 6).
notes.11:11: The Greek reads "Apoboch" (for Hebrew "Ahitub") and "opposite the house of God," rendering the Hebrew consonants for "ruler" as the preposition "opposite" (similarly in verse 22).
notes.11:15: Chapter 11 in the Septuagint is substantially shorter than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, omitting verses 16, 20-21, 28-29, and 32-35 as well as several genealogical and geographical clauses within the remaining verses.
notes.11:17: The Greek reads "Obeb" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Abda," and omits the intervening clauses detailing Mattaniah's lineage and Bakbukiah.
notes.11:25: The Greek reads "Kiriathar" (for Hebrew "Kiriath-Arba") and "Gala" in verse 31 (for Hebrew "Geba"), while verse 30 ends simply "and they encamped in Beersheba."
notes.12:2: The Greek text here has the truncated dative phrase "of Malluch" and omits verses 4–6; similarly, verse 9 consists solely of "For the divisions," and verse 18 is absent.
notes.12:8: The Greek reads "Machaniah" (for Hebrew Mattaniah) and "over the hands," reflecting a reading of the Hebrew term for thanksgivings as "hands."
notes.12:15: Throughout verses 15–22, several proper names preserve distinctive Greek readings, including Are, Mannas, Adadai, Ganathoth, Edio, Abed, Isdeiu, and the additional name Joa in verse 22.
notes.12:25: Instead of listing the gatekeepers, the Greek reads "when I gathered the gatekeepers"; in verse 27, "thanksgivings" translates the Greek transliteration "tholatha" (from Hebrew todot).
notes.12:37: The Greek reads "Gate of Praise" (for Hebrew Fountain Gate) and plural "cities of David," omits verses 38 and 40–41, and in verse 44 reads "leaders of the cities" where the Hebrew has "fields of the cities."
notes.13:5: "grain offering" renders the Greek transliteration "manaam" (from Hebrew minchah); in verse 9, the Greek instead reads "the manna."
notes.13:19: The Greek omits "until" before "after the Sabbath" (literally "not to be opened after the Sabbath") and omits the explicit object after "stationed."
notes.13:25: "You shall not give... nor take" renders the Semitic oath construction in Greek, literally "If you give... and if you take."
notes.13:29: "kinship" translates Greek "anchisteia," where the translator read the Hebrew root for defilement as the root for kinship or redemption.
notes.13:31: "firstfruits" renders the Greek transliteration "bakchouria" (from Hebrew bikkurim), and the Greek closes with "O our God" rather than "O my God."
